steps: Check codes & approvals
Install to CAN/CSA-B365 and local code; the local building officials approve the installation. Don't install in any fireplace or connect to an air distribution duct or system.

Install to CAN/CSA-B365; the local building officials have the final authorization, so discuss the installation with them before beginning.

Before starting, confirm the stove and chimney connector meet every clearance to combustibles and that the floor protection is adequate. The data plate on the back of the stove carries the safety-testing information, the certified testing laboratory and the installation requirements.

Do not install in any fireplace. Do not connect to any air distribution duct or system.
Unpack, fit legs + heat shield
Take the legs out of the stove, lift it off the pallet and lay it on its back. Unscrew the heat shield from the underside, then fit the legs and heat shield together with the same fixing bolts.

Flatten the outer packaging on the floor as a protective work surface. The heat shield must go on at the same time as the legs, using the same fixing bolts. Lift the stove upright without putting excess load on the back legs.

The 1410B weighs 75 kg. Two people are recommended for assembly and installation.
Maker's website: Gross Weight 215 lbs.
Check loose parts
Confirm the center grate and the firebricks haven't shifted in transit and the air control works freely. Poker, ceramic flue connection gasket and riddling tool are usually in the ashpan or firebox.
Verify the chimney
Dedicated flue in a code-approved masonry chimney with flue liner or a listed type HT factory-built chimney; 6" minimum internal diameter; independently secured, not supported by the stove.

Never connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance (several flues may share one stack, one flueway per appliance). HT chimney standard: UL-103-1985 (2100º F) for the USA, ULC S-629 (650ºC) for Canada.

Internal dimensions of the connector and chimney: not less than 6 inches diameter (or equivalent cross section) and not significantly larger. At least 16 feet of chimney above the stove, flue collar to top, is recommended (not required).
Set top or rear outlet
The flue collar ships on the top plate. For rear venting, knock out the round panel in the rear heat shield, swap the blanking plate and flue collar, then push down and tighten the enclosed screws.
Fit the chimney connector

6" single wall (24 gauge or heavier, not galvanized) or listed double wall. At least three screws at the stove and each joint, sealed airtight; slope up 1/4 inch per foot; no more than two 90 degree turns.

Horizontal run: 3 feet (1 metre) recommended maximum; total length no longer than 8 feet (2.5 metres); in horizontal runs keep 18 inches from the ceiling. Use mild bends (45º rather than 90º) and keep every part accessible for cleaning.

Don't pass the connector through an attic, closet or similar concealed space. For a combustible wall or ceiling, refer to local codes and the chimney manufacturer's instructions.
Clearances + floor protection
Position the stove to the single- or double-wall clearance table (and the alcove limits if recessed), on a non-combustible ember pad: 16" front and 6" sides of the door and ash openings in the US.
Fresh air + surroundings
Add a fresh air inlet of 2 square inches (1250 square mm) unless the room has enough natural air leakage. Keep furniture 30 inches away; a smoke detector in the stove room is recommended.
First fire
Keep the first fire small so the paint cures and the plates settle; ventilate the room. Operate only with the door fully closed; the minimum low burn rate is factory-set and must not be altered.

panels.title: Smoke spills / poor draft
items: Smoke or fumes when lighting or reloading → poor draft, almost certainly
Fire simply won't respond → poor draft; ask the stove supplier about upgrading the flue system
In a very few cases → not enough fresh air getting into the room
Stove suddenly sluggish → soot fall around the flue collar or in the flue/chimney
Back-puffing and sluggishness → overly dry wood that has turned gray

panels.title: Over-firing
items: Any part of the stove or the chimney connector glows → over-firing
Flue temperature above 450° C (750°F) → over-firing, premature wear
Baffle distorted by an over-fire → still works, efficiency compromised; replace
Fast internal wear → persistent heavy firing, soot and ashes left to accumulate

panels.title: Dirty or misting glass
items: Logs too large or not split
Combustion temperatures too low, or stove run too slowly
Wood spits or sizzles and the glass persistently mists up → wood not properly seasoned

panels.title: Gasket & grate wear
items: Door hard to close, or air leaking in around it → hardened door gasket; fire less controllable
Ash allowed to build up toward the underside of the grate → traps heat, premature grate failure

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Morsø recommends lighting top-down: it's the most environmentally friendly way, and it keeps soot off the glass. Build the fire right on the firebox floor (no andirons), and not too close to the door glass.

  1. Lay about 2-4 lbs of dry kindling sticks, with two firelighters placed directly under the top layer of kindling.
  2. Open the air fully: turn the spinner (the upper air control on the door) 4 turns counterclockwise from closed.
  3. Light the fire. Then close the door most of the way, leaving it open an inch or two to let in plenty of air.
  4. Once the chimney has warmed through, after 5-10 minutes, close the door. A good bed of embers forms in a further 15-20 minutes.
Stay with the stove the whole time the door is open. Never use gasoline, gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or any other liquid or chemical to start or freshen up a fire. Keep all such liquids away from the stove while it is in use.

Your very first fire

Keep it small, so the paint can cure and the stove's main plates can settle into position. The paint gives off some fumes while it cures, so ventilate the room. For that first lighting, use a 5-6 inch layer (2-4 pounds) of dry kindling to build up a bed of ash on the firebox floor.

air.title: Using the air control
air.html:
Your stove has two air supplies. Only one of them is yours to adjust.

Primary airUpper control on the door (the spinner): you set this
Secondary airTwo rows of holes in the steel baffle: constant, can't be changed
Lower door controlFixed, for decoration only

Spinner settings

Fully open4 turns counterclockwise from closed
Medium burn1-2 turns counterclockwise from closed
ClosedMinimum low burn rate (a small gap stays open)

Primary air also washes down the inside of the door glass at high speed, which helps burn the gases the fire gives off. Before you close the spinner fully, let the fire burn at medium for about 15 minutes so it's properly established.

The rule of thumb: less heat means less wood and less air; more heat means more wood and more air. Either way, keep a good layer of embers.

The minimum low burn rate is set at the factory. Don't alter it, or try to get more heat by changing the air control's range. It's against federal regulations.

reload.title: Reloading the fire
reload.html:
Reload while there are still plenty of live embers, adding a modest layer of wood each time.

  1. Use the poker to spread the embers across the firebox floor, bringing plenty toward the front.
  2. Lay 2-3 pieces of wood on the embers, leaving half an inch (1 cm) or more between pieces. The recommended load is 4-5 lbs (2-3 pieces).
  3. Close the door and leave the primary air fully open.
  4. After a few minutes, set the air control for the heat you want.

Make sure there's a good layer of embers first: the new wood should light within 2 minutes. If logs don't ignite, in an extreme case the flue gases can ignite, which risks damage or injury.

Always keep a 1-1.5 inch (2-3 cm) layer of ash on the floor of the firebox.

Note: p. 14 gives the maximum recommended load as 2 kg/h/5.5 lbs (approx. 3 split logs); p. 24 says to use no more than 2 - 2.5 kg when refuelling.

wood.title: Choosing and seasoning wood
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only: well seasoned, dry and split. The stove is listed for wood only, so don't burn other fuels, garbage or flammable fluids.

Lengthmax 10 inches (25 cm)
Maker's website: Log Size 12".
Thicknessapprox. 3 to 3.5 inches (7-8 cm)
Weight per piecearound 2 lbs
Moistureno more than 20%
Note: p. 11 gives the split thickness as approx. 3 to 3.5 inches (7-8 cm) in section; p. 24 says the fuel must be split and 8 - 12 cm thick.

Seasoning

Stack wood under cover in an airy spot where air can move through each piece. Some softwoods season in one good summer; harder woods such as oak, maple and elm can take up to 18 months. Seasoned wood feels light and shows cracks running out from the center at the ends. If it spits or sizzles and the glass keeps misting up, it isn't dry enough, and wet wood also cuts efficiency.

Avoid very dry wood that has turned gray: it can cause back-puffing and sluggish burning. The Morsø Moisture Meter (part # 62929900) checks moisture.

Never burn driftwood from the sea (its salt can cause corrosion) or construction wood that may be treated with chemicals.

overfire.title: Signs of over-firing
overfire.html:
Do not over-fire the stove. Over-firing can cause a house fire or permanently damage the stove. If any part of the stove or the stove pipe glows, you are over-firing.

Check the pipe temperature

The Morsø Flue Gas Thermometer (part # 62901200) attaches magnetically to the stove pipe about 20 cm (8") above the stove's top plate and reads the pipe's surface temperature. Measured 20 cm above the stove:

Normal firing (average)approx. 300° C (550°F)
Must not exceed450° C (750°F)

Going above that limit counts as over-firing and can wear the stove out early.

Note: p. 14 prints the flue-temperature limit as 450° C with 750°F alongside; those two figures are not the same temperature.

How to avoid it

  • Don't load more wood than recommended (see Reload the fire).
  • Don't alter the air control's range to get more heat.
  • Persistent heavy firing wears the inside of the stove quickly. An over-fire can distort the baffle: the stove still works, but efficiency may suffer, so replace it as soon as possible.

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
• The stove is hot while it's working. Keep children, clothing and furniture away: touching it can burn skin.
  • Keep furniture at least 30 inches away, and keep the same 30 inches clear of things like drying clothes, newspapers and firewood.
  • Never use gasoline, gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or freshen up a fire, and keep all such liquids away from the stove while it's in use.
  • Run the stove with the door fully closed. Never leave it unattended with the door open, because gas and flame can be drawn out of the opening.
  • Never burn overnight.
  • Don't use the stove if the door glass is damaged.
  • Fit a smoke detector in the room with the stove. Some areas also require carbon monoxide detectors. Put at least one smoke detector on each floor, close to bedrooms and away from the stove, so a puff of smoke while you reload doesn't set it off.

If you have a chimney fire

  1. Close the air control.
  2. Get everyone out of the house.
  3. Call the Fire Department.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Whenever you do maintenance on the stove, always protect yourself: wear safety goggles and gloves.

Run the stove at the right temperatures and there should be little or no dirt on the glass. Dirt that settles while you light the fire mostly burns off as it heats up.

For heavier deposits that won't burn off, use Morsø glass cleaner on cold glass, following its instructions. Never use abrasive cleaners on the glass.

Why glass gets dirty

  • Wood that's too wet or not well seasoned
  • Logs too large, or not split
  • A fire burning too cool, or run too slowly
Don't clean the glass while it's hot. If the door glass is broken or damaged, stop using the stove and replace it right away with Morsø's high-temperature ceramic glass from your Morsø dealer.

To avoid breaking the glass, don't strike it or slam the door. Old ceramic glass can't go in ordinary glass recycling: hand it in at a recycling station as ceramic glass.

The painted body

Keep the heat-resistant Senotherm paint clean with a vacuum's soft brush attachment or a lint-free cloth. If it turns slightly gray over time, Morsø touch-up spray paint is available from your stove supplier. Ventilate the room well the first time you fire after touching up, while the paint cures.

ash.title: Emptying the ash
ash.html:
Empty the ash pan daily or as needed. Ash that builds up toward the underside of the grate traps heat and can make the grate fail early.

Whenever you do maintenance on the stove, always protect yourself: wear safety goggles and gloves.

  1. With the door closed, work the grate with the riddling bar.
  2. Open the door and use a shovel or the poker to stir excess ash through the slots in the grate, down into the ash pan.
  3. Lift out the ash pan, keeping it level.
  4. Tip the ash into a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Set the closed container on a noncombustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything combustible.
  5. Put the ash pan back and close the door.

If you bury or spread the ashes, keep them in the closed container until every cinder has cooled.

Never empty the stove while it's in operation, and never use a household or shop vacuum cleaner to remove ash.

Over the summer

Ash left in an unused stove soaks up moisture, and moisture means rust. After the heating season, clean the stove out thoroughly and leave the spinner slightly open so air can move through. A desiccant such as kitty litter in the ash pan helps; remove it before the heating season. A chimney cap keeps rain out, but don't block off the flue completely.

chimney.title: Chimney, creosote & yearly checks
chimney.html:
Burning wood slowly makes tar and vapors that condense in a cool chimney as creosote. If it ignites, creosote makes an extremely hot fire, so inspect the stove pipe periodically and keep the chimney clean.

Whenever you do maintenance on the stove, always protect yourself: wear safety goggles and gloves.

  • To start with, check for soot above the baffle plate and around the flue outlet every month or so.
  • If the stove suddenly turns sluggish, check for a soot fall around the flue collar or in the chimney.
  • A good routine: clean the flue all the way to the top after each heating season, and inspect it before the next season for bird's nests or other blockages.

Before each heating season

  • Clean the chimney and stove pipe thoroughly, inspect them for damage and replace damaged sections. A mason repairs a masonry chimney.
  • Check the door gasket for wear or compression. Replace it if the door gets hard to close or air leaks in around it (a Morsø rope gasket kit is available).
  • Check the glass for cracks, and the door and handles for tightness.
  • Lubricate the hinges and closing mechanisms once a year or as needed, with copper grease or another heat-resistant grease.

Can't inspect or clean it yourself? Contact your Morsø dealer or a professional chimney sweep.

warranty.title: The Morsø guarantee
warranty.html:
If your stove was supplied by an authorised Morsø dealer, Morsø offers a 10-Year Manufacturers Guarantee against manufacturing defects in any of the stove's main exterior body parts.

Not covered

  • The flame-path equipment: ashpan, grate, firebricks, glass, baffle and flue collar
  • The ceramic rope
  • The paint finish

The flame-path parts take the full heat of the fire, so one or another will need replacing from time to time as routine maintenance. Your Morsø dealer sells them all. Replace damaged parts as soon as possible to avoid further damage, and always use original Morsø spare parts.

Register your new stove online on Morsø's US customer-service page.

This is a summary. The guarantee certificate and registration details are on the manual page linked below.

specOutput.title: Heat output & efficiency
specOutput.html:
Heat delivery12,115 to 24,733 Btu/hr
Average efficiency73.5% higher heating value (B415.1)
EmissionsMeets EPA limits for wood heaters sold on or after May 15, 2020
ListingPFS TECO, Portland, Oregon · Report F20-579
Test standardsUL-1482-2011 (R2015) USA · ULC-S627-00 Canada

The output range is "under specific test conditions". Listed for burning wood only.

It is against federal regulations to operate this heater in a manner inconsistent with the manual's operating instructions; it needs periodic inspection and repair.

specFlue.title: Flue & chimney
specFlue.html:
Connector & chimney IDNot less than 6 inches diameter (or equivalent cross section); not significantly larger
ChimneyCode-approved masonry with flue liner, or listed type HT factory-built
HT standardUL-103-1985 (2100º F) USA · ULC S-629 (650ºC) Canada
HeightAt least 16 feet recommended (not required), flue collar to chimney top

One flueway per appliance: never share a chimney flue with another appliance. The flue system must be independently secured, not supported by the stove. Don't install the chimney directly at the outlet; a chimney connector is required. Too large a flue lets the gases cool, making the stove sluggish or unpredictable. Roof construction, large trees nearby and high altitude can affect draft and height: consult a chimney sweep or Morsø dealer.

Top or rear outlet

From the factory the flue collar is on the top plate, prepared for the enclosed 6 inch adapter, and a round blanking plate closes the rear exit behind the rear shield plate. For rear venting, knock out the round panel in the rear heat shield plate to reveal the cast iron plate, untwist the blanking plate and flue collar and swap them, then push down and tighten the enclosed screws.

specConnector.title: Chimney connector
specConnector.html:
Diameter6 inches (150mm)
Single wall24 gauge or heavier steel (24 MSG black or blue); no galvanized
Double wallTested and listed for solid fuel
Horizontal run3 feet (1 metre) recommended max
Total lengthNo longer than 8 feet (2.5 metres)
SlopeUp 1/4 inch per foot (20 mm per metre) toward the chimney
TurnsNo more than two 90 degree
Horizontal runs18 inches from the ceiling

Secure with a minimum of three screws to the stove and to each adjoining section, and seal every joint so the system is airtight from the heater to the chimney outlet. Form one continuous section, use mild bends (45º rather than 90º), keep the run short and direct, and keep every part accessible for cleaning. Don't pass the connector through an attic, closet or similar concealed space, and avoid combustible walls and ceilings where possible. Wear gloves and protective eyewear when drilling, cutting or joining sections.

p. 6 refers to "the sections on Wall Pass-Throughs", which this manual doesn't contain. For a combustible wall or ceiling it points to local codes and the chimney manufacturer's instructions.

specClear.title: Clearances · single-wall connector
specClear.html:
Standard residential installation, integral rear and bottom shields, top or rear vent, single-wall connector. USA in inches, Canada in mm.

A. Sidewall to unit20" · 510 mm
B. Backwall to unit16" · 405 mm
C. Cornerwall to unit14" · 355 mm
D. Sidewall to connector25" · 635 mm
E. Backwall to connector18" · 455 mm
F. Cornerwall to connector20" · 510 mm

The table gives no value for G (unit to ceiling) or H (floor to ceiling). Increase distances for heat-sensitive materials, and make sure wallpaper or decorations can't fall toward the stove. Next to non-combustible materials, a gap of 4 inches or more is recommended for cleaning and heat circulation.

specClearDW.title: Clearances · double-wall connector
specClearDW.html:
Standard residential installation, integral rear and bottom shields, top or rear vent, double-wall connector. USA in inches, Canada in mm.

A. Sidewall to unit20" · 510 mm
B. Backwall to unit6" · 150 mm
C. Cornerwall to unit14" · 355 mm

The double-wall table shows dashes for the connector clearances (D, E, F) and for G and H.

specAlcove.title: Alcove installation
specAlcove.html:
W. Minimum alcove width56" · 1420 mm
D. Maximum alcove depth24" · 610 mm
G. Alcove ceiling above stove top36" · 915 mm

From the manual's alcove clearance table (USA / Canada). The text gives no other alcove requirements.

specFloor.title: Floor protection
specFloor.html:
The stove meets CAN/ULC-S627 for installation on a combustible floor and needs no radiant floor protection. A non-combustible pad is still required for falling embers.

Front16" · 450 mm
Right side6" · 200 mm
Left side6" · 200 mm
Backnot given (USA) · 200 mm

USA: non-combustible material, extending beneath the heater and 16" to the front and 6" to the sides of the fuel loading door and ash removal openings.

Canada (CSA B365): a continuous, durable, non-combustible ember pad beneath the appliance, extending at least 450 mm (18 in) beyond any side with a door and 200 mm (8 in) beyond the other sides; on the door side it runs the full width of the appliance plus 200 mm (8 in) each side. Less than 200 mm (8 in) from a wall, the pad need only reach the base of the wall. Not on top of carpet unless structurally supported against displacement and distortion.

specAir.title: Fresh air & surroundings
specAir.html:
Fresh air inlet2 square inches (1250 square mm) of free air space
Furniture30 inches recommended minimum
Movable combustibles30 inches (drying clothes, newspapers, firewood)

A dedicated fresh air inlet is needed unless there is sufficient ambient air leakage via doorways, windows and the like, particularly in a well-sealed room or where an extractor hood or ventilation system disturbs the natural air pressure. Don't place it on a wall usually subject to negative pressure from normal wind patterns, or directly across the room from the stove (cold draft).

If acid-washing the masonry around the stove, protect the stove surface with an acid-proof cover.

Canada: do not install in a transportable building / mobile home.

conflicts.issue: Split-wood thickness: p. 11 says approx. 3 to 3.5 inches (7-8 cm) in section; p. 24 says the fuel must be split and 8 - 12 cm thick.

Maximum fuel load: p. 14 prints '2 kg/h/5.5Ibs (approx 3 split logs)', and 2 kg and 5.5 lbs are not the same weight; p. 24 says no more than 2 - 2.5 kg per refuelling. p. 13 recommends a 4-5 lbs load (2-3 pieces).
Maximum flue temperature is printed as '450° C (750°F)' on p. 14; the Celsius and Fahrenheit figures are not the same temperature, so the limit is ambiguous.

review.notes: One manual (Morsø doc 72145211, dated 03.02.2025 on p. 24). Pages 7 and 22 have no extractable text (probably drawings, e.g. the 'Typical factory-built or masonry chimney installations' figure and the clearance diagrams). The clearance, alcove and floor-protection tables (pp. 8-9) were transcribed from their text labels only; the drawing that shows where each lettered dimension is measured is not in the text. p. 6 refers to 'the sections on Wall Pass-Throughs', which this manual doesn't contain; the guide points to local codes and the chimney manufacturer's instructions as p. 6 does. p. 5 says 'A chimney connector is included with the heater', while p. 6 mentions only the enclosed 6 inch adapter and tells the installer which connector to use; confirm what ships in the box (the guide doesn't claim a connector is included). The p. 17 inspection sentence is garbled ('- at least once a year. Inspect every month.'), so the guide gives only the monthly soot checks and the after-season cleaning routine. No troubleshooting chart or error codes in the manual: fault panels come from the draft-conditions (p. 14), over-firing (pp. 13-14, 16), dirty-glass (pp. 14-15), gasket (p. 17) and grate (p. 17) text. Not in the manual, so not checked against the catalog: heating area, emissions g/hr, firebox volume, height/width/depth, kW output, outside-air kit. The catalog item number does not appear in the manual; the p. 19 exploded-diagram title block is for 'Morsø 1400' (drawing from 2013). Written differently in the manual: '1-1.5 inch' is printed '1-1,5 inch' (p. 12); '5.5 lbs' is printed '5.5Ibs' (p. 14); 'kitty litter' is printed 'kitter litter' (p. 18); 'UL-103-1985 (2100º F)' is printed with a trailing period. The guarantee (p. 23) is one paragraph plus online registration; its exclusions come from p. 16. No French-only or font-offset text.
